question: Antigen presentation of extracellular pathogens by antigen presenting cells requires endocytosis of the antigen, followed by the degradation in the acidic environment of the formed phagolysosome. Should the phagolysosome become unable to lower its pH, what is the most likely consequence?

options.opb: Deficient presentation of pathogens to CD4 T-cells
options.opc: Deficient presentation of pathogens to CD8 T-cells

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Impaired phagolysosome acidification -> Inability to degrade antigens -> Deficient presentation of pathogens to CD4 T-cells -> 80% CHAIN: Impaired phagolysosome acidification -> Inability to degrade antigens -> Deficient presentation of pathogens to CD8 T-cells -> 75% CHAIN: Impaired phagolysosome acidification -> Inability to degrade antigens -> Deficient expression of B7 -> 80%
analysis: If the phagolysosome becomes unable to lower its pH, it would lead to deficient degradation of the antigen, affecting the presentation of pathogens to CD4 T-cells which are crucial for initiating the adaptive immune response.
